social_circle.name: Cody Jensen

demographics.occupation: Residential construction framer at a local Coeur d'Alene contractor

background.how_they_met: Met in 7th-grade gym class in Coeur d'Alene; bonded over fishing and dirt bikes through middle and high school.
background.why_close: Long-running fishing partnership, shared rural-Idaho upbringing, and a track record of being the one person Tucker actually talks to when he's struggling — Cody is the friend who noticed Tucker was checked out during his dad's surgery and dragged him out for wings.

interests: smoking weed at the fire pit on weekends
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Casual, lots of lowercase, abbreviations ('lol', 'k', 'yep'), drops fish photos and dad-memes; voice memo when driving home from a job site; rare punctuation.

shared_activities: Fishing on Lake Coeur d'Alene every other weekend in summer
Weekend fire-pit hangouts with occasional weed and cigars
Wings/beer nights when one of them needs a break
social_circle.communication_frequency: daily (or near-daily) — short threads about gear, weather, and weekend plans
recent_text_topics: Locking in opening-day plans for spring/summer fishing now that the weather's turning; arguing about which boat ramp to use.
Hazel turning 3 — Cody sending videos, Tucker pretending to be unimpressed but saving them.
Asking Tucker to come help frame a backyard shed for cash on a Saturday; running joke about Tucker quoting 'union rates'.
Checking in after Tucker's dad's PT appointments — Cody quietly making sure Tucker isn't going dark again like in October.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q07: 'My buddy Cody, I've known him since like seventh grade — he works construction now, married with a kid. We fish together pretty much every other weekend in the summer.' Q07 follow-up: 'Little girl, Hazel. She's three.' Q39: 'Maybe once a month, on a weekend night, usually with Cody when his wife's out with her friends.' Q44: 'Cody finally noticed and dragged me out for wings and that helped.'

social_circle.name: Hannah Baker

demographics.occupation: Nursing student at North Idaho College (part-time barista at a downtown coffee shop)
demographics.location: Coeur d'Alene, ID (lives with parents off 15th Street)
demographics.education: High school diploma; currently in pre-nursing coursework at North Idaho College

background.how_they_met: Tucker's younger sister; grew up in the same house off 15th Street.
background.why_close: Day-to-day sibling closeness reinforced by both being involved in helping their parents through their dad's back recovery and their grandma's decline. Hannah is the family's designated 'smart one' and Tucker is her steady older-brother sounding board.

key_traits: occasionally anxious — a softer version of their mom
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Long texts with proper punctuation, lots of question marks and exclamation points, uses some emojis (🙃, 😩), forwards TikToks Tucker never watches, occasional FaceTime.

shared_activities: Sunday family dinner at Mom's house around 5 PM
Visiting Grandma Patricia at Hayden assisted living together a couple times a month
Helping at Dad's house — Tucker doing yard/snow, Hannah doing meal prep with Mom
social_circle.communication_frequency: daily, mostly short bursts plus a longer evening exchange a couple times a week
recent_text_topics: Hannah venting about an anatomy professor and asking Tucker to quiz her on bones over Sunday dinner.
Coordinating who's bringing cinnamon rolls to Grandma this weekend and how she seemed last time.
Dad's PT progress — comparing notes since Hannah sees him daily and Tucker doesn't.
Teasing Tucker about a girl one of her friends thinks he should meet; Tucker stalling.
Sending him TikToks of bad TIG welds and asking 'is this you?' as an inside joke.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q01 follow-up: 'Yeah, Hannah. She's nineteen, lives with my folks still, doing some classes at North Idaho College. We text a lot, get dinner on Sundays at my mom's place most weeks. She's the smart one in the family, going to be a nurse.' Q15: 'Sunday is family dinner at mom's around five.' Q17: 'I check in on my grandma at the assisted living place twice a month.'

social_circle.name: Lisa Baker

demographics.occupation: Part-time bookkeeper for a local HVAC company (works from home most days)
demographics.location: Coeur d'Alene, ID (15th Street family home)
demographics.education: High school diploma + some community college (did not complete)

background.how_they_met: His mother; Tucker has lived in or visited the same family home his entire life.
background.why_close: Lisa is Tucker's primary emotional anchor and his most-trusted source of health information. She is also currently the household's main caregiver for both Ron (post-surgery) and Patricia (dementia), and Tucker is her practical right hand — and her midweek phone call when she needs to vent.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Full sentences, proper capitalization, lots of 'sweetie' and 'love you', occasional misplaced emoji, sometimes forwards long Facebook posts; tends to call rather than text for anything heavy.

shared_activities: Sunday family dinner she hosts at 5 PM
Coordinating care for Ron (post-surgery) and Grandma Patricia
Tucker mowing Dad's lawn April-October and plowing the driveway in winter
social_circle.communication_frequency: daily light texts; a long phone call every Sunday morning plus one midweek check-in call from Tucker
recent_text_topics: Reminders about Sunday dinner menu, asking if he can pick up rolls or sour cream on the way.
Updates on Ron's PT progress and pain levels; Lisa forwarding paperwork from the surgery payment plan.
Patricia's assisted-living facility called — small dementia incident — Lisa worried, Tucker calming her down.
Sending Tucker articles about GED prep and the certified production technician program, and bragging to him about a Facebook post about him fixing a neighbor's snowblower.
Gentle nagging that he's overdue on a dentist visit and 'really, Tucker, the hearing test'.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05: 'My mom, Lisa, she's a sweetheart, calls me every Sunday morning whether I want her to or not.' Q35 follow-up: 'I try to call her midweek just to chat, not just on Sundays.' Q42: 'Honestly? Mostly my mom — she's a worrier and reads up on health stuff.' Q103-Q104: bookkeeper part-time at a small local HVAC company. Q46: 'My mom has dealt with anxiety on and off for years, she's on some medication for it.'

social_circle.name: Brett Halverson

demographics.occupation: Service advisor at the Toyota dealership in Coeur d'Alene
demographics.location: Coeur d'Alene, ID (lives with Tucker in the Government Way rental)
demographics.education: High school diploma + a 9-month automotive service course

background.how_they_met: Classmates at Coeur d'Alene High School; reconnected as adults when Brett needed a roommate two years ago.
background.why_close: Two years of daily proximity in a shared house, plus a longer high-school history. They aren't deep talkers but they're each other's go-to for car help, house logistics, and Sunday Seahawks games. Brett is the moderate-political middle ground in the house — Tucker respects that they don't get into it.

key_traits: a little checked-out since he started dating Kayla seriously
personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Short, transactional texts ('door code?', 'milk?', 'fridge'), occasional meme, drops 'lol' a lot; voice memos when he's at the dealership and can't type.

shared_activities: Watching Seahawks games at the house on Sundays
Splitting groceries, utilities, and yard chores; occasional grill nights with Devin
Brett helping Tucker source parts and do brake jobs on the truck
social_circle.communication_frequency: multiple times a day (most of it household coordination); a longer Sunday-football thread
recent_text_topics: Heads-up that Kayla's staying over Thursday + Friday this week, can Tucker grab eggs.
Heating bill came in absurd again; arguing whether to call the landlord in Spokane or just wait it out.
Brett offering wholesale pricing on a new set of brake pads from the dealership parts counter.
Group-chat banter with Devin about the kitchen being a war zone and whose turn it is to take the recycling.
Trash-talking each other's fantasy football picks now that the draft conversations are starting early.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q11: 'One's a guy named Brett, he's twenty-four, works at the Toyota dealership in service. We've known each other since high school... We'll watch Seahawks games together on Sundays.' Q13: 'Brett's girlfriend Kayla stays over maybe two or three nights a week.' Q24 follow-up: 'Brett, my roommate, he's more middle-of-the-road and we don't really get into it.' Q59: heating bill spikes in winter / landlord slow to fix things.

social_circle.name: Marcus Reilly

demographics.occupation: Lead welder at Northwest Metal Works
demographics.education: High school diploma + Journeyman Welder certification

background.how_they_met: Coworkers at Northwest Metal Works since Tucker's first year there; Marcus took Tucker under his wing on the TIG side once Tucker 'locked in' after Dale's ultimatum.
background.why_close: Mentor-friend dynamic that has outgrown its workplace origin — they grab beers after shift, talk politics (mostly agree), and Marcus is the most credible voice Tucker has on the realistic path to his Journeyman Welder cert and shop ownership dream. The friendship is personal enough to live on SMS rather than only on the shop floor.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in short complete sentences, no emoji, drops welding terminology, sends grainy phone photos of bead work and asks 'what's wrong here'; the occasional dark joke about shop politics.

shared_activities: Beers after work at a bar near the shop a couple Fridays a month
Occasional weekend rides out to scout hunting spots
Side cash welding jobs — Marcus throws Tucker the overflow
social_circle.communication_frequency: 3-4x per week — mix of after-hours shop talk, hunting plans, and Tucker asking welding questions for his cert prep
recent_text_topics: Walking Tucker through which Journeyman Welder cert path actually pays off in North Idaho vs. the ones that don't.
A side gig welding a custom truck bumper for a guy in Hayden — Marcus offering to split the job and the cash.
Eye-rolling about the latest shop-floor argument over immigration; both agreeing Hector is the best welder in the building.
Sending photos of TIG beads from a stainless job Tucker is practicing on at the shop after hours.
Plans to drive up and scout a new elk unit before tag draws this year.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q07: 'Then there's Marcus, he's a guy from the shop, he's about thirty, he's kind of taken me under his wing on the welding side. We'll grab a beer after work sometimes.' Q24 follow-up: 'Cody and me will, Marcus at work will. We mostly agree which makes it easier.' Q70: 'I'll do a side cash job once in a while welding something for somebody.' Q77: 'Marcus and Hector are who I'm closest with.'
